images.caption: Figure 2:RoboArchitectturns a frozen policy into a performant robotic agent without updating its weights: a coding model iteratively refines the harness from execution traces.Starting from a bare policy (VLA),RoboArchitectevolves a robotic agent equipped with auxiliary tools and persistent memory. The right side illustrates experiment conditions (Section4.1) that test how well the evolved harness generalizes.

Figure 3:Evolved control routines fix concrete failure patterns.Each row shows an episode under an earlier harness (starting with bare VLA policy) on the left, and under the revisedRoboArchitectharness on the right. Row (a) shows detecting and clearing arm jams, (b) synthesizing missing motion primitives, (c) rescaling contact forces, and (d) redirecting to target objects instead of memorized locations.Fig.5shows more examples. See discussions on these revisions inSection4.3andAppendixA.

Figure 4:Persistent memories emerge from harness evolution and inform action decisions.Each row illustrates one form of memory mechanism; rows (a) and (b) show reusable execution experience, (c) task and environment context, and (d) embodiment-specific calibration. See discussions on these memories inSection4.4andAppendixA.
